LESSON: STORYTELLING LISTENING

Grade: Grade 2
Subject: LITERACY ACTIVITIES
Strand: Word and sentence By the end of the sub-strand, the  Learners practice hearing 
Topic 1.3: Storytelling LISTENING

SECTION 1: WELCOME

Hello! This is a study lesson on Storytelling LISTENING. Read the explanation, follow every worked example, then do the practice. This is original CBC Learn content written from KICD outcomes — not a copy of a commercial textbook.

Big question: Why do we tell LISTENING learner should be able to: family, and home from peers, resource persons, stories?

SECTION 2: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

By the end of this lesson, you will be able to:

1. appreciate morals taught through and teachers
2. show empathy with people, places, (traditional and modern) listened to and things  Learners record their stories and play them for

SECTION 3: STUDY NOTES (READ AND LEARN)

WHAT YOU ARE STUDYING: STORYTELLING LISTENING
Subject: LITERACY ACTIVITIES · Grade: Grade 2
This is a learner study lesson (not a teacher guide). Read every part, follow the models, then practise.

BIG PICTURE
Storytelling LISTENING helps you succeed in LITERACY ACTIVITIES. You will understand it, practise it, and use it at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

KEY FACTS: STORYTELLING LISTENING
Language skills grow by daily practice: listen carefully, speak clearly, read every day, write neatly.
Model → guided practice → independent practice.
Always use complete sentences when writing answers.

PART 1: Appreciate morals taught through and teachers

What this means
In this part you learn to appreciate morals taught through and teachers. You will use ideas from at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: appreciate morals taught through and teachers.
2. Listen, speak, read, then write using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Model reading: Read a short paragraph about “Storytelling LISTENING”, then retell it in 3 sentences.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can appreciate morals taught through and teachers. Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 2: Show empathy with people, places, (traditional and modern) listened to and things  Learners record their stories and play them for

What this means
In this part you learn to show empathy with people, places, (traditional and modern) listened to and things  Learners record their stories and play them for. You will use ideas from at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: show empathy with people, places, (traditional and modern) listened to and things  Learners record their stories and play them for.
2. Listen, speak, read, then write using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Model speaking: Say 4 clear sentences about Storytelling LISTENING to a partner.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can show empathy with people, places, (traditional and modern) listened to and things  Learners record their stories and play them for. Write or say your answer clearly.

PUT IT TOGETHER
Close your notes and say aloud: what Storytelling LISTENING is, one example, and one way you will practise this week.

SECTION 4: QUICK EXAMPLES

Example 1: Read a short paragraph about “Storytelling LISTENING”, then retell it in 3 sentences. (skill: appreciate morals taught through and teachers)

Example 2: Say 4 clear sentences about Storytelling LISTENING to a partner. (skill: show empathy with people, places, (traditional and modern) listened to and things  Learners record their stories and play them for)

SECTION 5: PRACTICE NOW

1. Write 5 sentences (or show 5 clear steps) that teach Storytelling LISTENING to a classmate.
2. Practise this skill: appreciate morals taught through and teachers.
3. Practise this skill: show empathy with people, places, (traditional and modern) listened to and things  Learners record their stories and play them for.
4. Make one local Kenya example of Storytelling LISTENING from your county, market, farm, or school.
5. Mark your own work: What did you get right? What will you redo?

SECTION 6: WORK TO DO (HOME / REVISION)

1. In your exercise book, make a one-page revision sheet for Storytelling LISTENING: meaning, 3 examples, 5 practice items.
2. Teach a parent/guardian or younger sibling one part of this lesson (2 minutes).
3. Answer in writing: Why should a Grade 2 learner study Storytelling LISTENING?
4. Prepare for the quiz: cover the Remember box and recite it.

SECTION: THINK ABOUT IT

1. Why do we tell LISTENING learner should be able to: family, and home from peers, resource persons, stories?
2. Why are stories different thematic stories  Learners respond to questions on the stories told important to us?

SECTION: REMEMBER

1. Know what Storytelling LISTENING means in your own words.
2. Use local Kenyan examples, not only definitions.
3. Practise in small steps, then check your work.
4. Be able to: appreciate morals taught through and teachers.
5. Be able to: show empathy with people, places, (traditional and modern) listened to and things  Learners record their stories and play them for.

Now complete the Revision Quiz. Open Answers only after you finish.

— CBC Learn · Original study notes from KICD outcomes (Strategy 2)
